HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD ?Court No. - 83 Case :- CRIMINAL MISC ANTICIPATORY BAIL APPLICATION U/S 438 CR.P.C. No. - 3075 of 2023 Applicant :- Banarasi And 5 Others Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Shyam Shankar Shukla Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.

Heard Sri Ajay Shnkar, learned Advocate holding brief for Sri Shyam Shankar Shukla, learned counsel for the applicants as well as Sri V.K.S. Parmar, learned A.G.A. for the State and also perused the material available on record.

2. The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicants in F.I.R./Case Crime No. 24 of 2014, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 IPC, Complaint Case No. 16 of 2014, Police Station Khairgarh, District Firozabad, with a prayer to enlarge them on anticipatory bail.
3. As per prosecution story, the applicants are stated to have impersonated the deceased father Laakhan Singh in a partition suit filed in the year 2011.
As such, the applicants had committed the forgery in the said court.
The FIR was instituted in the year 2014 against the applicants and other co-accused persons.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicants has stated that the applicants are maliciously being prosecuted in the present case due to ulterior motive and have the apprehension of their arrest.
The applicants have nothing to do with the said offence as alleged by the prosecution.

Learned counsel has further stated that due to some clerical mistake in the office of the Advocate concerned, instead of writing down the name of the co-accused person, Sehdev, the name of his father was transcribed as to be the person, whose thumb impression was put in the said petition.
Learned counsel has next stated that owing to the said fact coming to light, the investigating officer was pleased to file a closure report in the said act.

On the protest petition of the informant, the case was treated as complaint case and later on, even the said complaint was also dismissed under Section 203 Cr.P.C.
5.

Learned counsel has next stated that the informant moved a criminal revision before the Session Judge, Firozabad, whereby the court was pleased to allow the said revision and had remanded it back to the concerned Magistrate, who had summoned the applicants and other co-accused persons vide order dated 13.8.2018.
Learned counsel has further stated that the said FIR itself is misconceived as is evident from the said closure report and the order of Magistrate concerned dismissing the said complaint.
Learned counsel has next stated that the applicants had filed a petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C., but could not succeed in it.
There is nothing on record to suggest that the applicants have committed the said offence.
It is next stated that the informant had failed twice in his attempt to get the applicants prosecuted.
6. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicants to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against them.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicants have also been touched upon at length.
It is further submitted that the applicants have cooperated in the investigation.
They have not misused the liberty granted to them.

In case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicants is allowed, they will not misuse the liberty and shall cooperate with trial.
7.
On the other hand, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicants.

12. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicants shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
